back: The cable or wireless signal that carries data between devices on a network.
The amount of data a medium can carry per second, measured in bits per second.
The weakening of a signal as it travels along a medium; it limits the distance data can be sent.

front: Twisted pair cable: one advantage, one disadvantage?
back: Cheap, thin and flexible; but short range (about 100 m) and the lowest noise immunity.

front: Coaxial cable: structure and main benefit?
back: A copper core, insulation, braided metal shield and sheath; the shield gives better noise immunity than twisted pair.
Highest bandwidth, longest distance with little attenuation, immune to electrical interference (and hard to tap).
notes: Disadvantages: most expensive; fragile; needs skilled joining.

front: Wireless media: one advantage, one disadvantage?
back: No cables, so easy for mobile users and easy to expand; but less secure, shared bandwidth and affected by walls and interference.
Time (s) = amount of data (bits) ÷ bandwidth (bits per second).
notes: Use the same units: megabits with Mbit/s.

front: Why does fibre ignore electrical noise?
back: It carries light, not electricity, so electromagnetic interference cannot corrupt the signal.
